l.i: Frangens in teneros languida verba s-
Quicquid habet docti schola, quicquid Roma decori,
Hoc Pietas uno junxit utrumque libro:
Pulveris at Schola quicquid habet, vel Roma
Hoc Bona mens toto pellit utrumque libro.
Cerne vices rerum! fidei quondam inclyta famâ
Roma fuit, qua nunc destruit ecce fidem:
Nec non & pariter quo Roma vetusta superbit
Eloquio liber hic destruit ecce novam.

page.notes: The verse lines are italic; the first word of each line of the Latin couplets is in larger capital form in the scan (Q, H, P, C, R, N, E). Line breaks in verse are given as printed with hyphenation "de-" / "cori" kept as one word "decori". Small specks and stains on the page are not transcribed.
